rationale: V4 background patch representations significantly improve normalized nuisance/sensitivity ratios and natural preference, but raw score variations have a smaller scale. The frame/all-pairs view retains 0.4922 of the origin mean background-switch response on dev. A fixed gain of 2 approximately restores that response scale, while expanding nuisance by the same factor. This cannot create the positive normalized improvement.
methods: Apply the same gain to every one of the six v4 patch ablations; retain every original score and negative result.
selection: Among calibrated region candidates passing every dev gate, select the smallest full-foreground MAE on all 142 native bases, while requiring the 34-base diagnostic to remain below 0.01. Natural preference labels are not used to fit the score gain. Freeze the final primary before test scoring.
clipping: Recompute scores and human-preference ties after clipping; never assume ranks are unchanged. Report counts of raw values outside [0.5,1].
test_status: NOT RUN; all gains and choices are development-only
